contract.intent: Specify the RESOURCE/REGISTRY management pattern — the general design for 'configurable things that consumers reference': rules (ask/check/decide), ladders, adapters (providers/models), flows (step chains), bindings, surfaces. One registry per class = single source of truth; consumers read; config manages; no layer duplicates. The rule registry is instance #1; the root-cause fixes (tech-stack rung, resolution provenance, high-impact-defaulted) are its initial content. Produces a NEW locked contract (logical name: resource-registry).
acceptanceCriteria: resource-registry-spec.md artifact exists — the general pattern (registry = SST per class; consumers reference; config manages; versioned)
Registry schema frozen: {id, category, kind, definition|ref, config:{enabled, priority/severity, params}}

Instances enumerated: ask (ladders incl. tech-stack rung) · check (validation rules incl. high-impact-defaulted) · decide (resolution ladder + provenance discussed|defaulted|inferred) · adapters · flows · bindings · surfaces
The rule: a rule/resource lives in exactly ONE registry; no layer duplicates (the seam-killer)
Management surface: one place to list/add/version/enable/tune; consumers read the registry, never hardcode
Spec locked (type=spec, upstream ann-system-design + architecture); indexed; resolvable
requiredInputs: Root-cause analysis (this session): the tech stack fell through the seam — no layer owned 'what to ask'; the fix = one registry, all consumers reference
